acceptance_checks: No daily profile can be confirmed without the required session context being present for that profile.
The New York reversal profile cannot appear unless London first failed to reach the relevant higher-timeframe anchor.
The New York manipulation profile cannot confirm without a current-day range sweep plus the selected post-sweep shift proxy.
Seek-and-destroy must block directional expansion-style expectations until price truly holds outside the range.
The script must keep the session logic bar-close confirmed and avoid unbounded multi-timeframe requests.
Profile overlap handling must remain explicit and configurable rather than silently favoring the last branch evaluated.
Backtest results must include spread, slippage, commission, and fee assumptions before performance is treated as credible.
Historical execution must assume next-bar-open entry after a confirmed bar-close signal instead of intrabar lookahead fills.
If stop and target touch in the same bar, assume the stop prints first unless lower-timeframe replay evidence proves the target filled first.

Target expectation state pointing toward continuation delivery, previous-day liquidity, failed swing targets, or rotational equilibrium.

open_implementation_questions.question: What is the cleanest first-pass rule for deciding whether London already completed too much of the day's expansion for New York continuation to remain valid?
How should overlapping session features be ranked when a day partially resembles both New York manipulation and New York reversal?
What is the strictest useful first-pass CISD proxy for session-profile confirmation without relying on discretionary chart reading?

pine_translation_hints: Prefer bar-close confirmation over intrabar discretion.
Keep lower-timeframe requests focused and finite.
Represent structure and invalidation as explicit state objects.

provisional_proxies.logic: Use a directional close through the opposing candle series as the first session-shift proxy, optionally strengthened with displacement.
Treat London as having completed too much of the day once it consumes more than the configured portion of the expected daily expansion window.
Break profile conflicts by preferring the higher-timeframe-anchor path first, then the direct current-day sweep path, then the rotational seek-and-destroy filter.
Classify the day as seek-and-destroy once the range sweeps both sides and returns toward equilibrium or the daily open at least the configured number of times.

signal_pipeline.logic: Track daily open, Asia range, London range, and the earliest New York interaction points so the day can be classified by session sequence instead of isolated candles.
signal_pipeline.name: Session Range Build

signal_pipeline.logic: Detect when London forms the daily wick and shifts direction, then reject the continuation path if London already appears to have completed most of the expected daily expansion.
signal_pipeline.name: London Reversal and Completion Filter

signal_pipeline.logic: Split the New York path into manipulation versus reversal depending on whether the session is sweeping the current day's range or finishing a missed higher-timeframe run first.
signal_pipeline.name: New York Manipulation and Reversal Branch

signal_pipeline.logic: Require a first-pass CISD or directional close-through-opposing-series event, then require a protected swing when that filter is enabled before treating the profile as confirmed.
signal_pipeline.name: Session Shift Confirmation

signal_pipeline.logic: When the day keeps sweeping both sides of the range and returning toward equilibrium or the daily open, demote directional expectations into a seek-and-destroy filter until a true outside hold appears.
signal_pipeline.name: Seek-and-Destroy and Rotation Filter

signal_pipeline.logic: Use the confirmed profile to choose continuation delivery, previous-day liquidity, failure swing targets, or rotational mean-reversion expectations, and invalidate the profile when the corresponding session structure breaks.
signal_pipeline.name: Profile Targets and Failure Management

transitions.condition: London forms the daily wick away from the intended close and begins the shift needed for a New York continuation profile.
London confirms the shift and New York continues in the same direction without London already completing too much of the day's range.
London stays mainly consolidative and New York approaches the live day's range for a sweep setup.
New York sweeps the day's range and confirms the opposing delivery path through the selected shift proxy.
London fails to reach a higher-timeframe anchor that New York is still positioned to complete.
New York completes the missed run into the higher-timeframe anchor and confirms the reversal shift.
London and New York keep rotating across the same session range without directional hold.
Price stops rotating and holds outside the active range with structural confirmation.

machine_checks: Mark prior-day high and low as reversal anchors
Measure whether the higher-timeframe candle sweeps a prior-day extreme and closes back inside or rejects from it
Require lower-timeframe confirmation before execution mode is active
rules.name: Reversal-day bias is framed from previous day highs or lows plus lower-timeframe confirmation

machine_checks: Compute equilibrium as midpoint of previous day range
Detect whether lower-timeframe closes remain on the correct side of equilibrium
Require continuation through the previous day directional objective
rules.name: Continuation-day bias uses prior candle closure plus equilibrium respect

machine_checks: Compute body size and opposing wick ratio
Classify whether the candle closes near its directional extreme or near its open
Switch expected target model based on small-wick versus large-wick classification

machine_checks: Store higher-timeframe bias as a state variable
Reject lower-timeframe execution signals that oppose the active bias
Allow configurable execution timeframe mapping by session or user selection

open_questions: What is the cleanest first-pass rule for deciding when a brief pause becomes a true consolidation instead of just a small pullback inside expansion?
How should the project rank direct sweep evidence versus SMT substitute evidence when both can stand in for range manipulation?

machine_checks: Track whether price remains internal between a stable range high and range low
Measure whether price keeps reverting toward range equilibrium instead of displacing decisively
Block directional entries while consolidation remains unresolved
rules.name: A consolidation is an internal range between a defined high and low where directional intent is unresolved

machine_checks: Require a sweep or validated SMT substitute before manipulation logic is enabled
Require closure through the opposing candle series before entry eligibility
Reject setups that sweep a side but keep rotating across the full range
rules.name: The preferred consolidation setup is a sweep of one side of the range followed by confirmation away from the swept side

machine_checks: Require an outside close before treating the move as a valid breakout
Reject breakout continuation if price closes back inside the range
Promote retest entries only after the broken boundary holds as support or resistance
rules.name: A breakout continuation is valid when price leaves the range, holds outside it, and confirms on the retest

machine_checks: Track equilibrium reversion while price remains internal to the range
Lower expansion expectations after repeated false breakouts or two-sided sweeps
Block continuation-style entries while no directional protected swing exists
rules.name: While consolidation remains unresolved, equilibrium and range-rotation behavior should dominate expectations

open_questions: What is the cleanest first-pass rule for deciding whether London already completed too much of the day's expansion for New York continuation to remain valid?
How should overlapping session features be ranked when a day partially resembles both New York manipulation and New York reversal?

machine_checks: Detect whether London forms the session extreme opposite the intended daily close
Require a London structure shift before enabling New York continuation logic
Block New York continuation setups when London has already completed the expected daily expansion
rules.name: London reversal and New York continuation profiles use London to form the daily wick and New York to deliver the body

machine_checks: Detect whether New York sweeps beyond the active London range
Require a post-sweep close through the opposing candle series before entry eligibility
Track previous-day highs or lows as the first expansion targets after confirmation
rules.name: New York manipulation profiles sweep the current day's range during New York and then deliver in the opposite direction

machine_checks: Require London to fail to reach the higher-timeframe anchor before New York reversal logic is enabled
Require New York to sweep into the anchor and then confirm with displacement plus CISD
Store the post-CISD swing as the active invalidation reference
rules.name: New York reversal profiles occur when London falls short of a higher-timeframe level and New York completes the run before reversing

machine_checks: Detect whether London sweeps both sides of the Asia range without directional hold
Demote directional expectations when price keeps rotating back through London equilibrium or the daily open
Block expansion-style entries while no directional protected swing forms outside the range
rules.name: Seek and destroy profiles are rotational non-opportunity days unless false breakouts can be faded back toward equilibrium

open_questions: What numeric ratio should separate a small opposing run from a large opposing wick across the main timeframe pairs?
How close to the open should a candle finish before it is treated as a reversal-style candle instead of an expansion candle?

machine_checks: Compute the wick opposite the candle direction and compare it against the body
Require the close to finish near the directional extreme rather than near the open
Classify the candle as expansion-supporting only when the opposing wick remains small relative to the full range
rules.name: A small opposing wick with a large body supports expansion in the candle direction

machine_checks: Classify candles with dominant opposing wicks as poor expansion candidates
Downgrade continuation expectations when the close finishes too close to the open
Switch the target model toward the open or nearby liquidity after a large opposing run
rules.name: A large opposing wick with a smaller body favors reversion toward the open or nearby liquidity

machine_checks: Compute the wick midpoint from the body edge to the wick extreme
Track whether subsequent closes remain on the respected side of the midpoint
Flip the wick state from respected to disrespected once a close breaches the midpoint
rules.name: Respect or disrespect of the wick midpoint determines whether rejection is holding or failing

machine_checks: Classify the higher-timeframe candle first as expansion-supporting or reversal-leaning based on wick behavior
Gate lower-timeframe expansion reads on the higher-timeframe wick classification
Downgrade lower-timeframe continuation setups when the parent candle shows large opposing rejection
rules.name: Higher-timeframe wick behavior should govern whether lower-timeframe structure is read as expansion, reversal, or range

open_questions: What numeric tolerance around the 0.5 line should count as valid equilibrium respect versus a true close-through failure?
How should multiple points of interest inside the respected half be ranked before lower-timeframe confirmation appears?

machine_checks: Compute equilibrium as the midpoint between wick high and wick low
Reject body-only midpoint calculations for this topic
Persist the selected midpoint until the reference range is intentionally replaced
rules.name: Equilibrium is measured from wick high to wick low, not from candle bodies

machine_checks: Track whether price is holding in the correct half of the reference range
Flag loss of continuation bias when closes move through the wrong side of equilibrium
Keep the continuation bias active only while the expected half remains respected
rules.name: In expansion conditions, respect of the correct half of the range defines the directional bias

machine_checks: Project the previous day's equilibrium into the new session
Reject continuation when lower-timeframe closes occur beyond equilibrium in the wrong direction
Allow minor probing around the midpoint only until the close-based failure condition appears
rules.name: A continuation day is framed from the previous day's equilibrium and confirmed by lower-timeframe closes that stay on the correct side

machine_checks: Require both a point of interest and lower-timeframe confirmation before promoting an equilibrium reaction into an entry setup
Allow fallback to newly created liquidity only if it remains inside the respected half of the range
Mark the setup as context-only when equilibrium is respected but no confirmation appears
rules.name: Equilibrium becomes tradable when the respected half also contains a point of interest and lower-timeframe confirmation

machine_checks: Detect liquidity sweep beyond local swing
Detect confirming close beyond reference candle series

machine_checks: Default stop equals protected swing extreme
Optional aggressive stop equals candle body reference
Allow trailing stop updates from newer protected swings
rules.name: Protected swings provide structural stop placement

machine_checks: Maintain most recent protected swing by direction and timeframe
Reject entries that oppose active higher timeframe structure
rules.name: Trade direction should follow the most recent valid protected swing logic

machine_checks: Represent anticipated and confirmed protected swings as distinct states
Require originating timeframe close for confirmation
Flag pre-confirmation entries as aggressive mode

machine_checks: Require a higher-timeframe directional classification before evaluating lower-timeframe entries
Reject lower-timeframe continuation signals that directly oppose the higher-timeframe bias
Downgrade all lower-timeframe setups when the higher timeframe is still unresolved consolidation
rules.name: The higher timeframe sets the directional bias and lower timeframes should not override it on their own

machine_checks: Require an intermediate-timeframe point of interest that agrees with higher-timeframe direction
Require a directional closure or CISD before promoting the setup to execution-ready state

rules.name: The intermediate timeframe must confirm the higher-timeframe bias with structure, a point of interest, and a directional closure

machine_checks: Gate lower-timeframe entry logic behind an explicit higher-plus-intermediate alignment flag
Treat lower-timeframe structure as execution refinement instead of independent direction selection

rules.name: The lower timeframe is for entry precision only after the higher and intermediate timeframes are already aligned
pine_inputs_needed: alignment flag between higher and intermediate timeframes

machine_checks: Require at least two expansion-supporting timeframe flags for the clean-trend classification
Elevate the setup quality when all three monitored timeframes align
Downgrade or defer the setup when any parent timeframe prints a non-expansion-supporting candle
rules.name: A clean trend requires aligned expansion-supporting candles across at least two timeframes
